Definition: properly, to press, i.e. (figuratively) to be pungent or vehement; to irritate
BiblicalUsage: mârats is to press hard, to be pungent and vehement, to irritate. In Job 6:25 Job asks how forcible right words are, and what his friends' arguing reproves, and in Micah 2:10 the people are told to arise and depart, because the land is polluted and will destroy them with a sore destruction. The word is pressure that stings.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârats warns me that right words can cut, and that a polluted rest is no rest at all.
